prompts: Build the shell of 'Studio Manager', a client & invoice management app for a small design studio. Requirements: (1) Replace the template placeholders: the NavBar brand must read 'Studio Manager', with nav buttons 'Dashboard', 'Clients', and 'Invoices' switching views via useHistoryView; keep the dark-mode toggle. (2) The Dashboard view is home: a short welcome heading and a hint of what's coming. (3) The Clients and Invoices views exist but hold no data yet — each shows an EmptyState block ('No clients yet' / 'No invoices yet'). (4) Seed a prototype clients collection through the persistence seam (src/lib/storage.ts createStore) with 3 example clients (name, email, company) and list them on the Clients view as simple cards — do NOT read or write localStorage directly in a view. Keep `npm run build` passing.

Graduate Studio Manager to a REAL backend so data lives in a database on a server. Use the project's backend pack — apply it with the ApplyPack tool and follow the backend skill; do NOT hand-write the server scaffold, Prisma setup, or migrations. Then: (1) Add a Client model to prisma/schema.prisma: id Int autoincrement, name String, email String, company String (optional), createdAt DateTime default(now()). Run the migration. (2) Expose it via the server's RESOURCES registry as 'clients'. (3) Seed the database with exactly 6 clients, one of them named 'Aurora Textiles' with email 'hello@auroratextiles.example' — either via the pack's prisma/seed.ts (npm run db:seed) or by seeding on server boot when the clients table is empty; the seed must repopulate a freshly reset database without manual steps. (4) Switch the frontend persistence seam to the API-backed store WITHOUT changing any view. The dev proxy (/api → :8787) already exists; the server reads PORT from env (default 8787). Data must persist across server restarts.

Wire the Clients view properly to the API: (1) a loading state while fetching (SkeletonList or an equivalent skeleton, not a spinner-only blank), (2) an ErrorState block with a 'Retry' button when the API call fails, (3) the EmptyState only when the API returns zero clients, (4) clicking a client opens a Client detail view showing name, email, company, and the date added, with a way back. Fetch through relative '/api/...' URLs only.

Client management: (1) a 'New client' button on the Clients view opening a form (name, email required with inline validation messages; company optional) that POSTs to the API and returns to the updated list, (2) an 'Edit' action on the client detail view reusing the form with values prefilled, PUT on save, (3) a 'Delete' action on the detail view with a confirmation dialog before DELETE. Server side: POST and PUT must reject a missing/empty name or email with HTTP 400 and { error }.

Invoices, end to end: (1) Prisma models — Invoice: id Int autoincrement, clientId Int relation to Client, status String ('draft' | 'sent' | 'paid'), createdAt DateTime default(now()); InvoiceItem: id Int autoincrement, invoiceId Int relation to Invoice, description String, qty Int, unitPrice Float. Migrate. (2) API: GET /api/invoices returns invoices each carrying its items, its client's name as clientName, and a server-computed total (sum of qty × unitPrice, rounded to 2 decimals). GET /api/invoices/:id likewise. POST /api/invoices accepts { clientId, status, items: [{ description, qty, unitPrice }] } and must 400 with { error } when items is missing/empty or clientId is unknown; PUT updates status and/or items (recompute total); DELETE removes the invoice and its items. (3) Extend the seeding (same idiom you used for clients — prisma/seed.ts or seed-on-boot): exactly 9 invoices across the 6 seeded clients with createdAt dates spread over the last 3 months — exactly 3 'draft', 3 'sent', 3 'paid'. (4) UI: the Invoices view is a DataTable block with columns Client, Status (a Badge), Total, and Date; a 'New invoice' button opens a form with a client selector, a status selector, and a line-items editor ('Add line' button, per-line description/qty/unit price inputs and a remove control, and a live computed total); clicking a row opens an invoice detail view with its line items and a 'Delete' action.

Search and filtering, server-side: (1) GET /api/clients gains ?search= — case-insensitive substring match on name, email, and company. (2) GET /api/invoices gains ?status= (draft|sent|paid) and ?clientId=. (3) BREAKING CHANGE, both list endpoints now return the envelope { items: [...], total: <count of ALL matches> } instead of a bare array — update every frontend call site. (4) UI: a search input on the Clients view with the exact placeholder 'Search clients…' filtering as you type, and a status filter (chips or tabs: All / Draft / Sent / Paid) on the Invoices view. Search/filter state must combine with everything already built.

Pagination, server-side, on both list endpoints: ?page= (1-based) and ?perPage= (default 10, max 50); the envelope's total stays the FULL filtered match count so the UI can compute page count. UI: 'Previous' / 'Next' controls and a 'Page X of Y' caption under both the Clients and Invoices lists (the DataTable caption slot is a good home). Out-of-range pages return an empty items array, not an error. Search/filter must reset to page 1.

A real Dashboard: (1) API: GET /api/stats returns { clients, invoices, outstandingTotal, paidTotal, revenueByMonth } where clients/invoices are row counts, outstandingTotal is the summed total of 'sent' invoices, paidTotal the summed total of 'paid' invoices (both rounded to 2 decimals), and revenueByMonth is an array of { month: 'YYYY-MM', total } for the last 6 calendar months (missing months included with total 0) counting sent+paid invoices by createdAt. (2) UI: the Dashboard view becomes 4 StatCard blocks — 'Clients', 'Invoices', 'Outstanding', 'Revenue' — computed from /api/stats (money formatted with exactly two decimals), plus a ChartCard block titled 'Revenue by month' rendering revenueByMonth as a bar chart.

Authentication: (1) Prisma User model: id Int autoincrement, email String unique, passwordHash String, createdAt DateTime default(now()). Passwords are hashed with node:crypto scrypt and a per-user salt — never stored or compared in plaintext. (2) API: POST /api/auth/register { email, password (min 8 chars) } → 201 and a session cookie; POST /api/auth/login → 200 and a session cookie, 401 on bad credentials; POST /api/auth/logout clears the session; GET /api/auth/me → { email } with a valid session, else 401. Sessions may live in an in-memory Map keyed by a random token, delivered as an HttpOnly cookie named 'sid' (parse the Cookie header manually — no new dependencies). (3) Seed a user (same seeding idiom as before): owner@studio.local with password 'studio123'. (4) From now on EVERY /api/* route except /api/auth/* and /api/health returns 401 { error } without a valid session. (5) UI: when not signed in, the app shows only a sign-in screen built on the AuthCard block (email + password fields, a 'Sign in' submit button, an error line on failure); after sign-in the full app loads, the NavBar gains the signed-in email and a 'Sign out' action.

CSV export: (1) API: GET /api/invoices/export.csv (session required) responds with Content-Type text/csv; the FIRST line is exactly 'id,client,status,total,date' followed by one line per invoice (client is the client name; total with two decimals; date as YYYY-MM-DD). It must honor the same ?status= filter as the invoice list. (2) UI: an 'Export CSV' button on the Invoices view that downloads the file respecting the currently selected status filter.

Three hardening fixes, everywhere they apply: (1) Deleting a client that still has invoices must be refused — API returns 409 with { error } naming the invoice count, and the UI surfaces that message instead of removing the row. (2) Every money value anywhere (API totals, stats, CSV, and every UI surface) is rounded/formatted to exactly two decimals. (3) Server-side line-item validation: qty must be an integer ≥ 1 and unitPrice a number ≥ 0 — violations are HTTP 400 with { error }; the invoice form shows the message inline.

Final polish: (1) Run the TemplateAudit tool and fix EVERY hard finding until it reports clean. (2) Restyle the whole app to the 'luxe-dark' preset using the Restyle tool (preset operation) — do not hand-edit theme files. (3) Sweep the app for consistency: every list has loading/empty/error states, dark mode is coherent on every view, and the production build (`npm run build`) passes. State what changed in your final summary.
